Where we come from

“What makes a box isn’t
the equipment.
It’s the people.”

We trained in a box in France, then moved away — and so did our friends. What we missed was never the equipment: the energy of people training beside you, a coach whose advice landed, a WOD scaled to the level you were actually at. No recorded programme can put two people in a session together.

So Joris built the app we could not find: one that lets you train apart without training alone. The session is scaled to you, on the gear you own, and a friend is on the other phone. That is why we wrote the live 1v1 ourselves — and went head to head with friends in other countries. A leaderboard does not make you finish the set; the mate who pushes you and gives you grief does.

Then came the part we had not planned for. That mate had watched you do it — and nobody had a way to prove it.

What we wanted back

The energy of your friends, a coach whose advice lands, and a WOD scaled to the level you are at — in a garage, with one kettlebell.

What we built, unfunded

ohmGym. 240 commits since late August, 1,100 tests, live 1v1 video training.

What the witness unlocks

Iron Chain on Seeker. Your mate countersigns with a fingerprint in the Seed Vault — we know no other Solana app that does it. Set a goal, hit it, and the marker is yours for good: nobody can take it back, and nobody had to believe you.

The problem

Other apps paid people to move, took their word, and kept their history

They paid people to move

StepN and Genopets paid a token per step. When the money stopped, the people stopped. The ones still standing now live on insurers and corporate programmes, paid in ordinary currency.

Left with: a dead token

They take your word

Strava records what you declare, for 195 million registered athletes. A public link lets anyone look at a session. Nothing lets them verify it.

Left with: a screenshot

They keep your history

Ten years of sessions belong to the company that stored them. Change app, and the record does not come with you. There is nothing to export that anyone else would accept.

Left with: nothing at all

The fix is not a better reward. It is a record the user owns, that someone else can check.

Networks built on physical work do not win by handing out tokens. They win when someone needs that work verified, and pays to read it.

What Iron Chain is

A training app that writes proof you own to Solana

You train alone, or head to head with a friend, one phone each. When the clock stops, you both sign. The proof lands in your wallet, not in our database.

If we shut down tomorrow, you keep it. A stranger can verify it with a link.

The protocol underneath is open under Apache 2.0. Any app can issue and verify the same proofs.

Design target · the shipped screens are in the demo video

A human watching you train is the hardest witness to fool. The peer co-signs the proof.

4 / 14

How a proof holds up

Six signals, not a score

CodeSignalWhat it establishesCost to fake
DDeclared · the user logs the sessionNothing. It is the starting point.None
BBracketed · two in-app photos, hashed on the deviceSomething happened between t₀ and t₁Low to medium
MMeasured · heart rate, calories, steps over the sessionA body was under loadMedium
CCoherent · the heart-rate curve matches the declared effortThe effort matches the claimHigh
WWitnessed · a peer co-signs, present over live videoA human saw the sessionVery high
NNotarized · a verified coach co-signsA professional stakes their reputationHighest

"signals": ["D", "B", "M", "C", "W"]  ·  A proof carries the signals it actually has. Nothing more. The reader applies its own threshold.

Everyone else stops at D

Every fitness-on-chain project we know writes a self-declared session and calls it proof. We record D as what it is: a claim. Then we add the rest.

Why signals, not a score

A "level 3" ages badly. The day one signal is faked, every past attestation collapses with it. Signals don't: stop trusting B, and M, C, W stay readable on proofs issued years ago.

W is the signal Iron Chain is built around. A watch can go on someone else's wrist. A person watching you cannot. We know no other Solana app that puts a human witness in front of a session.

Mobile first

A workout is the real world. It takes a camera, sensors, and a friend on the other phone.

Live 1v1 video W · Witnessed

Two friends train together over WebRTC. It works today. A watch can go on someone else's wrist. A person watching you train cannot be faked. The peer co-signs.

Wearable sensors M · Measured C · Coherent

Health Connect reads calories, steps, resting heart rate and HRV. A claim becomes a measurement.

Camera capture in the app B · Bracketed

A photo at the start and at the end of the session, hashed on the device. Only the hash leaves the phone.

Together, these signals constrain each other. To fake a session you would need a heart rate curve between two photos taken in the app. You would have to train.

Only on Solana Mobile

Why Solana, and why the Seeker

Solana Attestation Service

The attestation standard of this ecosystem, a public good under Apache 2.0. Our schemas extend it.

Seed Vault

Hardware signing on the phone is a Solana Mobile primitive. A countersignature that costs a fingerprint exists only here.

Ownership that survives us

The attestation lives in the user's wallet. If Iron Chain shuts down, the proof remains and stays verifiable.

Mobile Wallet Adapter

The Solana Mobile standard for connecting a wallet on Android. Phantom and Solflare connect on a physical device, built since September 17.

Together, these four mean a duel needs no referee. Two friends, two phones, two fingerprints — and a result neither of them can edit afterwards. The goal you set becomes a marker nobody can take back, not even us. None of that works if the record lives in our database.

We built ohmGym on iOS first. The live 1v1 changed the plan: a session witnessed in real time needs a chain that can carry the proof and a phone that can sign it. So Solana Mobile gets this app first — before any app store, and the ecosystem is where it can go further than we could alone.

Only a hash goes on-chain. Health data and photos stay on the phone. Swiss company, Swiss and EU data protection law.

What comes next · what only Seeker can do

The co-signed duel, signed in the Seed Vault

During the hackathon, both players co-sign the duel result in the app. Next, that countersignature goes on-chain and into hardware.

Both players sign the result in the Seed Vault. A fingerprint each. One attestation carries both signatures, on the duel-result schema, on mainnet.

Health Connect adds calories, steps, resting heart rate and HRV. A claim becomes a measurement.

A duel starts from the lock screen, through a push notification. On screen, the countersignature reads “Certify Matt’s session”: one tap, one fingerprint.

A human witness and a hardware signature on each side. A reason for two people to own a Seeker.

Design target · the shipped screens are in the demo video

Accepted when

A duel between two Seekers produces one attestation on mainnet, co-signed by both through the Seed Vault, verifiable with the open verifier. Health Connect signals appear on devices that expose them.

Planned for the Seeker release, after the hackathon.

Traction · and how to run it

What exists today, and what starts now

The app, ohmGym by Iron Chain, runs on iOS TestFlight, internal. Iron Chain is the open standard underneath it. The first public release is the dApp Store.

The Android edition is signed with a dedicated dApp Store key and runs end to end on a Xiaomi, Android 16, since September 17.

MWA connects Phantom and Solflare on hardware. A finished session is written on devnet as a signed memo since September 14. Public protocol repository since September 15.

How it spreads. A duel takes two, so every player brings a partner. Every proof comes with a public link anyone can check: the Strava screenshot, made verifiable. Sharing your progression comes next.

The pilot is under way, self funded: ten testers who train in pairs for two weeks. We will publish the first results in early October, whether they are good or bad: sessions completed per tester, duels played, and who stopped and why.

How to run it

APK: the signed release in the submission. Any Android phone; a Solana wallet app in devnet mode (Phantom or Solflare).

Repository: ironchain-app/ohmgym, read access for the judges, build instructions in the README, no secret needed to compile.

Demo, 3 minutes, on a real device: a session, a duel, Finish, the signature in the wallet, the transaction on the explorer.

Live 1v1 with the team on request: the witness signal, experienced rather than read.

12 / 14

Public good

What the ecosystem keeps if Iron Chain disappears

We publish an open standard for verifiable physical activity under Apache 2.0: the proof-of-activity schema family on the Solana Attestation Service, plus TypeScript and Flutter SDKs. Public since September 15 at github.com/ironchain-app/ironchain-protocol.

The standard records which independent signals corroborate a claim: declared, bracketed, measured, coherent, witnessed, notarised. The reader applies its own threshold. A standard that hardcodes a level dies the day that level is defeated. One that records signals stays useful.

Who can use it without us

A fitness app whose users keep their history when they switch.

A challenge between friends that settles itself, with no referee.

A club or a community running a season nobody has to police.

A race organiser or a tournament that co-signs results.

Any Solana app that needs proof a human did something physical.
